title: 4 Top Dividend Stocks Yielding 4% or More to Buy Right Now for Passive Income
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: Consumer staples companies PepsiCo, McCormick, Hormel, and Clorox are trading near 52-week lows due to headwinds including changing consumer preferences toward healthier products, budget constraints, and rising costs. However, these companies offer attractive dividend yields (4.1%-5.7%) and have proven track records as dividend growers, making them potentially opportunistic buys for long-term dividend investors.

title: CAVA vs. Celsius: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares CAVA Group and Celsius Holdings as growth investment opportunities. CAVA, a Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant chain, shows strong traffic-driven growth with 31% revenue growth and 9% same-restaurant sales growth in Q2 2026. Celsius, an energy drink company, achieved 85.5% revenue growth in FY 2025 but disappointed in Q2 2026 with missed earnings estimates and compressed margins. The author recommends CAVA as the better long-term investment due to its solid unit economics and consistent execution, while noting Celsius faces risks from PepsiCo concentration and integration challenges.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong traffic-driven growth with 31% revenue growth and 9% same-restaurant sales growth in Q2 2026. Expanding unit economics, solid profitability with restaurant-level margins above 25%, and new locations outperforming expectations. Author explicitly recommends this stock as the better buy.

While showing impressive 85.5% FY 2025 revenue growth, Q2 2026 results were disappointing with missed earnings and revenue estimates, compressed gross margins, and sharply declining earnings. High customer concentration risk with PepsiCo representing 43.2% of revenue and ongoing legal challenges limit upside potential.

title: Dutch Bros vs. Celsius: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Anders Bylund
description: The article compares Dutch Bros and Celsius as growth stock investments in the shifting beverage market. Dutch Bros operates 1,225 drive-thru locations with 27.9% revenue growth and improving profitability (4.9% net margin), while Celsius achieved 85.5% revenue growth but declining earnings due to acquisitions. Dutch Bros trades at higher valuations but shows better earnings growth, while Celsius offers cheaper valuation and triple the free cash flow but faces heavy Pepsi distribution dependency. The author favors Dutch Bros for its combination of respectable top-line growth and rising profits.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company shows strong revenue growth (27.9%), improving profitability with net margin expanding to 4.9%, and positive earnings trajectory. Despite higher valuation multiples, the PEG ratio suggests reasonable value when accounting for growth expectations. The author explicitly recommends this stock over Celsius.

While Celsius demonstrates exceptional revenue growth (85.5%) and strong free cash flow ($323.4M), earnings are declining and net margin contracted to 4.3%. The company faces significant concentration risk with Pepsi accounting for 43% of revenue and integration challenges from acquisitions. Cheaper valuation is offset by operational concerns.

Mentioned as Celsius' primary distribution partner controlling 43% of revenue, representing both an opportunity and a significant risk factor for Celsius' business independence and decision-making autonomy.

title: Will PepsiCo's Q3 Turnaround Boost These ETFs?
author: Na
description: PepsiCo reported Q3 fiscal 2026 revenues of $25.27 billion and core EPS of $2.34, beating estimates, but faces margin pressure from rising commodity and energy costs. The company lowered its full-year core EPS growth guidance to 2.5-3.5% from 5-7% and plans additional cost-cutting measures. The results highlight PepsiCo's exposure through major consumer staples ETFs.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with revenue and EPS beats offset by declining margins, reduced guidance, and rising cost pressures. While the company demonstrated demand generation, the margin compression and lowered outlook indicate challenges ahead despite cost-cutting initiatives.
ETF holds 7.9% PepsiCo exposure. Sentiment reflects the mixed performance of its largest holding, with both positive earnings beats and concerning margin pressures affecting the fund's outlook.
